abstract.text:
Can any secrets still be shed by that much studied, uniquely integrable,
Elliptic Billiard? Starting by examining the family of 3-periodic trajectories and
the loci of their Triangular Centers, one obtains a beautiful and variegated gallery
of curves: ellipses, quartics, sextics, circles, and even a stationary point. Secondly,
one notices this family conserves an intriguing ratio: Inradius-to-Circumradius. In
turn this implies three conservation corollaries: (i) the sum of bounce angle cosines,
(ii) the product of excentral cosines, and (iii) the ratio of excentral-to-orbit areas.
Monge’s Orthoptic Circle’s close relation to 4-periodic Billiard trajectories is well-known. Its geometry provided clues with which to generalize 3-periodic invariants
to trajectories of an arbitrary number of edges. This was quite unexpected. Indeed,
the Elliptic Billiard did surprise us!

source_span.start_text: Can the Elliptic Billiard Still Surprise Us?

sections.summary: The paper opens by asking whether the elliptic billiard can still surprise us. It reviews prior studies and proofs that several triangle-center loci are ellipses, describes the authors' applet and video experiments, and identifies the breakthrough: the conserved inradius-to-circumradius ratio and Monge's orthoptic circle as a route to arbitrary N.
sections.title: Introduction: Can the Elliptic Billiard Still Surprise Us?

source_span.end_text: For N = 3 explicit expressions have been derived [9, 10].

sections.summary: Explains the elliptic billiard as an integrable Hamiltonian system and a special case of Poncelet's porism. It introduces Joachimsthal's invariant gamma, the confocal caustic, and the constant-perimeter property for N-periodic trajectories.
sections.title: Integrability, Joachimsthal Invariant, and Constant Perimeter

source_span.end_text: whose center coincides with the triangle’s Mittenpunkt.

sections.summary: Surveys N=3 triangle-center and derived-triangle loci. Major centers such as X1 through X5 have elliptic loci; Excenters also produce an ellipse; Intouch, Feuerbach, and Medial triangles produce non-elliptic loci; Extouchpoints and the Feuerbach point sweep the caustic; and the Mittenpunkt is stationary at the billiard center, yielding the Circumbilliard corollary.
sections.title: Triangle-Center Loci from Incenter to Mittenpunkt

source_span.end_text: Corollary 4 A 3-periodic family conserves the Excentral-to-Orbit area ratio.

sections.summary: Presents the central N=3 conservation law: the ratio of inradius to circumradius is invariant. From this it derives conservation of the sum of cosines, the product of excentral cosines, and the excentral-to-orbit area ratio.
sections.title: Constant Radii Ratio and Conservation Corollaries

source_span.end_text: This surprising phenomenon can be viewed here [19, pl#16,17].

sections.summary: Introduces a circular locus for the N=3 case: the intersection points Q1 and Q2 lie on a circle centered on the billiard. The radius can be written via aspect ratio, r/R, or 1/gamma, and the circle is identified with the Cosine Circle of the Excentral Triangle.
sections.title: Circular Locus for N=3

source_span.end_text: That is, z lies on the circle of radius 1/γ.

sections.summary: Generalizes the N=3 invariants to N>3 orbits using clues from the N=4 family. It proves a stationary generalized Mittenpunkt, generalized extouchpoints on the caustic, conservation of cosine sum and product, area-ratio conservation for odd N, and a circular locus with radius 1/gamma.
sections.title: Generalizing Invariants to N>3 Orbits

source_span.start_text: Can the Elliptic Billiard Still Surprise Us?

sections.summary: The paper opens by asking whether the elliptic billiard can still surprise us. It reviews prior studies and proofs that several triangle-center loci are ellipses, describes the authors' applet and video experiments, and identifies the breakthrough: the conserved inradius-to-circumradius ratio and Monge's orthoptic circle as a route to arbitrary N.
sections.title: Introduction: Can the Elliptic Billiard Still Surprise Us?

source_span.end_text: For N = 3 explicit expressions have been derived [9, 10].

sections.summary: Explains the elliptic billiard as an integrable Hamiltonian system and a special case of Poncelet's porism. It introduces Joachimsthal's invariant gamma, the confocal caustic, and the constant-perimeter property for N-periodic trajectories.
sections.title: Integrability, Joachimsthal Invariant, and Constant Perimeter

sections.summary: Surveys N=3 triangle-center and derived-triangle loci. Major centers such as X1 through X5 have elliptic loci; Excenters also produce an ellipse; Intouch, Feuerbach, and Medial triangles produce non-elliptic loci; Extouchpoints and the Feuerbach point sweep the caustic; and the Mittenpunkt is stationary at the billiard center, yielding the Circumbilliard corollary.

sections.summary: Presents the central N=3 conservation law: the ratio of inradius to circumradius is invariant. From this it derives conservation of the sum of cosines, the product of excentral cosines, and the excentral-to-orbit area ratio.

sections.summary: Generalizes the N=3 invariants to N>3 orbits using clues from the N=4 family. It proves a stationary generalized Mittenpunkt, generalized extouchpoints on the caustic, conservation of cosine sum and product, area-ratio conservation for odd N, and a circular locus with radius 1/gamma.
